rationale: Both independently rediscover the ground-truth reviewer's core theme (the 'shared' rotary helper isn't actually shared — sibling BNSD call sites in qwen3_code_predictor.py and the 310P patch weren't migrated), but X frames it correctly as blocking with a forced disjunction (predicate wrong vs. latent crash elsewhere) and backs it with concrete math, while Y buries the same finding as two 'minor' items with weaker verdicts (COMMENT, no severity differentiation). X also finds a genuine, previously-unflagged correctness bug (ndim!=4 falling through to the transpose branch) with a proposed one-line fix, and a non-contiguous output-tensor issue, giving it stronger actionability via concrete diffs/test additions. Y is broader but padded with process narration (Scan table, Validated checklist) and several thin nits ('add a one-line PR note') that add citation volume without proportional value. Neither candidate surfaces the ground-truth ask for a 3-way (BNSD/BSND/plain-torch) performance comparison, capping recall for both.
